findings.title: argon2i_32 accepts nb_blocks below the required minimum, causing out-of-bounds heap write and read in crypto_argon2
findings.evidence: argon2i_32 takes caller-supplied nb_blocks and writes it straight into crypto_argon2_config (line 328) and sizes the work area as nb_blocks*1024 bytes (line 345) without enforcing monocypher's documented precondition nb_blocks >= 8 * nb_lanes (monocypher.h:160; nb_lanes is hard-coded to 1 at line 330). In crypto_argon2, config.nb_blocks < 4 makes segment_size and lane_size collapse to 0 (monocypher.c:752-754), but the prefill loop unconditionally writes two full 1024-byte blocks, blocks[0] and blocks[1] (monocypher.c:776-782). With nb_blocks=1 the Python side allocated only 1024 bytes, so the blocks[1] write overflows the heap chunk by 1024 bytes with data derived from the caller's password/salt/ad; with nb_blocks=0 the allocation is malloc(0) (zero/NULL-sized) while 2048 bytes are written. For nb_blocks 0..3 the later 'last_block = blocks + lane_size - 1' (monocypher.c:902) becomes blocks-1, and store64_le_buf reads 1024 bytes before the work area (monocypher.c:911), which extended_hash then mixes into the returned digest - a heap out-of-bounds read/disclosure. For nb_blocks 4..7, segment_size=1 makes window_size underflow (monocypher.c:870-880), so block 3 is read before it is initialized. Any application that lets the memory cost (nb_blocks) come from outside - e.g. KDF parameters stored with a password hash or supplied through an API - reaches these unsafe operations by calling argon2i_32 with nb_blocks < 8; the resulting corruption/leaked bytes are directly observable through the return value.

findings.title: Unchecked malloc return value in argon2i_32 dereferenced as the Argon2 work area
findings.evidence: work_area = malloc(nb_blocks * 1024) (line 345) is never checked for NULL before crypto_argon2(hash, 32, work_area, ...) is called (line 347). An attacker-influenced nb_blocks (e.g. 2**30, a 1 TiB request, or any value that exhausts the process address space/memory limit) makes malloc return NULL, and crypto_argon2 immediately dereferences and writes through the pointer - 'load64_le_buf(blocks[l * lane_size + i].a, hash_area, 128)' at monocypher.c:781 (and the ZERO at monocypher.c:915) - producing a NULL-pointer dereference that crashes the process (denial of service). For nb_blocks=0, malloc(0) is implementation-defined and may also return NULL, which then gets dereferenced the same way.
